questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT one of Knuth's required properties of an algorithm?

options.text: It is written in a specific programming language
Finiteness — it terminates after finitely many steps
Definiteness — each step is precisely defined
Effectiveness — each step can actually be carried out

questions.explanation: An algorithm is language-independent. Finiteness, definiteness, input, output, and effectiveness are the required properties; the choice of programming language is not.

options.text: it halts with the specified output for every valid input
it returns the right answer for the inputs you tested
it runs in O(n) time or better
it never uses more than a constant amount of memory

questions.explanation: Correctness means halting and producing the specified output on EVERY valid instance — not just tested inputs, and independent of how fast or memory-light it is.

questions.prompt: Which statements about loop invariants are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: The invariant must be true before the first iteration (initialization)
If true before an iteration, it must remain true before the next (maintenance)
At loop termination, the invariant helps establish the desired result
A valid loop invariant guarantees the loop terminates

questions.explanation: Initialization, maintenance, and termination are the three parts. An invariant alone does NOT prove termination — you must separately show the loop ends.

questions.prompt: The three parts of a loop-invariant argument are initialization, maintenance, and ______. (one word)
questions.explanation: Termination uses the invariant, together with the condition that ended the loop, to conclude the property you wanted to prove.

questions.prompt: Put the three steps of a loop-invariant proof in the order you apply them.

items.text: Initialization: the invariant holds before the first iteration
Maintenance: each iteration preserves the invariant
Termination: the invariant yields the result when the loop ends

questions.explanation: You show it holds at the start, that every iteration keeps it holding, and finally that when the loop stops it gives the property you wanted.

questions.prompt: Match each term with its meaning.

pairs.right: One concrete input to a problem
What is assumed true when a routine is entered
A property preserved across every loop iteration

questions.explanation: A problem is the general spec; an instance is a specific input; a precondition is what must hold on entry; a loop invariant is preserved each iteration.
